newsitem.title: THAILAND: Chavalit to finalise Thai government in few days.
newsitem.headline: Chavalit to finalise Thai government in few days.

text.p: Thai premier-designate Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Tuesday he and his coalition partners had ironed out differences over the cabinet make-up and hoped to present a complete list for royal approval in the next few days.

Chavalit, the leader of the New Aspiration Party (NAP) which won the most seats in last week's general election, was officially named the 22nd prime minister by a royal decree issued by King Bhumibol Adulyadej on Monday.
He has formed a six-party coalition that will command a comfortable majority of 221 seats in the 393-member parliament.
For the last nine days Chavalit and his partners have been embroiled in fierce wrangling over how to share the various ministries.
A confident Chavalit told foreign reporters in his first briefing since becoming premier-designate that the major problems -- most dealing with economic portfolios -- had been worked out.

"It was solved already last night," he said with a wave of his hand when asked about the talk of continued rift over economic portfolios with the second largest coalition partner, the Chart Pattana Party.
Chavalit said he would name a group of experts led by respected economist Amnuay Viravan as finance minister to resuscitate Thailand's lagging economy.
Amnuay would also be in charge of all economic issues, while the Chart Pattana party would take charge of infrastructure, communications, industry and foreign affairs.
Chavalit said the cabinet list should be finalised and presented to the king within the next few days. The government should be sworn in around December 1, a top Chavalit aide said.
Although the government's top priority is the economy, Chavalit said he also planned to emphasise political reform in his administration and complete a new constitution.
"Thailand cannot wait one more day," he said, noting it would probably take several years for the process of writing a new charter. "Thai politics will need a long time to adjust or reform."
Chavalit also vowed to end rampant corruption that has plagued the Thai political scene for several administrations.
"No corruption. Leadership, strong and straight," he said when asked to define his new government.

"Thailand is now facing a serious crisis -- a crisis of confidence... Confidence will be restored when there is a perception that the right people are in the right jobs, and that they are working toagether as a united team for the benefit of their country," he said.

Chavalit, a 64-year old general and former army chief turned politician who has never kept his ambition to be premier a secret, said he never doubted he would finally reach his ultimate goal and get Thailand's top job.
"Last Sunday (November 17) was not a normal day for me," he said in a voice hoarse from the electoral campaign and negotiations over the past few days.
"I thought from the beginning we would get a lot of seats. But it almost caused me to have a heart attack."
